title: Why MP3 Cover Art Shows on One Player but Not Another
primary_question: Why does embedded MP3 cover art appear on one music player but disappear or show the wrong image in another?
source_title: How to Clean Up MP3 Metadata Before Organizing Music

fact_sources.supports: ID3v2.4 attached picture APIC frame supports format, picture type, description and binary image data, distinct from an external image file.
Mutagen ID3 reference documents APIC description uniqueness, multiple frames, ID3 version conversions and v2.3 save option.
FFmpeg MP3 muxer reference documents APIC attached-picture handling and ID3v2.3/ID3v2.4 support; it does not guarantee any particular music player display.

new_examples: Fictional Harbor at Dawn folder contains cover.jpg alongside 01-Arrival.mp3 but the MP3 has no APIC. After moving the MP3 alone to a phone the art vanishes. The guide isolates an external image from an embedded one by testing a saved file copy.

Fictional Night Ferry MP3 has two attached pictures, an obsolete thumbnail and a recent front image. Two players choose different images, so a reversible one-front-cover test copy distinguishes conflicting APIC selections from a codec or audio fault.
editorial_notes: Independent diagnosis of missing/wrong artwork across two players. Different user intent from the broad canonical MP3 cleanup checklist. References checked from source publishers on 2026-11-13. Link to ONNELLAB primary article returns HTTP 200. All cases clearly labelled fictional. No copied art, images, app endorsements or third-party text reproduced. No claim of a universal fix.
